title: Enforce descriptive hypothesis/confound/run labels over opaque short codes
body: Claim-tier IDs like H1, C1, m3, m2.7 are fine as internal references but add cognitive load when humans read claim reports, lint output, or conclude-gate feedback. Investigate enforcing or encouraging descriptive labels (e.g. 'H_information_symmetry', 'C_topology_coupling') alongside short codes, or requiring a `label` field in [[hypotheses]] and [[confounds]] blocks that is used in human-facing output (lint warnings, claim-coverage report, conclude verdict) while the short ID is used for machine cross-referencing. Could be a Tier-1 lint rule (warn if id matches /^[A-Z][0-9]+$/ with no label field), a scaffold default, or a claim validate check.
